title: B31 Freiburg: the Schuetzenallee-Tunnel's two tubes as one twin box (middle wall only where it fits)

frame.x: m east of the origin (local ENU tangent plane)
frame.z: geodetic height (m) as the DEM gives it; every z in this file, also the floors

t1.run_on: upstream/dev 241aae43 (tunnel.rs last changed in b82b6abf: 636, held)

key_values.reason: never a wall in a lane

key_values.field: rows where the built middle wall differs from the rule
key_values.reason: rule 7; the one row lies 0.01 m over the threshold

rules: rule 7: two box tubes whose walls come within TWIN_BOX_GAP_M 3 m (2 x portals.COVER_SIDE) are one twin box

its middle wall (0.6 m) stands only where both carriageways and the wall fit between the axes (spacing >= ca + cb + 0.6 m, here 3.25 + 3.25 + 0.6 = 7.1 m), else the row is one wide cell (open); never a wall in a lane (twin_wall_in_lane 0, twin_wall_end 0)
rule 8: no structure of one road inside the other's tube (tube_intrusion 0)

rule_vs_prototype.rule: T4: walls on the free edges of the tunnel faces, faces closer than 3 ft (0.9 m) merge into one hall; no twin logic
rule_vs_prototype.prototype: pairs of box tubes, a middle wall where it fits
rule_vs_prototype.here: the same result is expected: a middle wall exactly where both carriageways + 0.6 m fit

notes: twin_rows are the road tiles' tube rows (roadmesh.tunnel's sections as tunnelscan reads them) every 2 m: wall_left / wall_right are the lateral offsets of the section's walls (+ left of the road's direction), open_left / open_right whether the row has no middle wall on that side; rule_middle_wall the rule's answer from the axes alone (null where the rows are no twins: walls further than 3 m apart or floors more than 4.7 m apart).
Built vs rule: 1 row of 416 differs (westbound s 352.1: spacing 7.11 m vs the 7.10 m threshold, built open).

twin_open 2: the two open stretches (eastbound / westbound, about 100 m each near 47.9861, 7.8718, axes down to 6.4 m apart) are listed, not faults: the map's axes closer than their carriageways (OSM, fixed 2026-11-23, reaches the build with the next Overture release).
The boxes' reason is 'town' (TunnelProfiles.boxes checks town first); the twin layout is roadmesh's.
T1's record (t1_actual) on these strokes: lid / full runs by cover only; T4 decides the walls.

portal.s.reason: rule 2: the portal stands at the mapped end of the tagged range (the station of the mapped vertex; 1 m = the line's resampling); T1 rule P may move it outward only (X_MAX 30 m), never inward

portal.floor.reason: the prototype's floor at the mouth; the rule behind it: within 0.5 m of the road's own approach line (rule 2, PORTAL_END_HIGH_M / mouth_step), never a DEM sample over the mouth, never a neighbour's cutting

portal.roof_top.reason: floor + the section's height: a box 4.70 m clear + 0.80 m roof = 5.50 m, a full bore 6.80 m (roadmesh.TUNNEL_H), a major road's low arch 5.0 m

floor_at.reason: the prototype's floor (rule 3: the lower hull between the pins, sunk where the cover over the crown is under 1 m, rounded over 12 m); the maintainer's floor comes from prof.rs within its grade limits, so these are reference values, not targets

section.s0_s1.reason: rule 1: a tunnel is the tagged range (is_tunnel / is_covered / tunnel=*), per range; a joint between two mapped parts is where the map splits them

section.label.reason: box_town / box_twin (rule 6: a town tunnel under thin cover is a cut-and-cover box; rule 7 twins), bore, low_arch, gallery (rule 12), cutting (rule 4: an open level < 0 stretch); t1_code is T1's 0 gap / 1 lid / 2 full for the same stretch

stations.z_profile.reason: the prototype's built profile (the floor inside the tubes, the graded road outside): the z a profile solver would hand stroke_record

wall.top_at_mouth.reason: rule 5 (the user 2026-11-25): a town ramp wall's top at the mouth is the portal's top, then one even fall to the street level beside

wall.face_offset.reason: rule 5 (task 7n): the wall's inner face is flush with the opening's side (the tube's half width = carriageway half width + 1.2 m shoulder)

cutting.under_higher_side_16m.reason: rule 4: an open level < 0 stretch lies at least 1 m (CUT_BELOW_M) under the higher natural ground 16 m to either side (tunnelscan cut_at_grade); never at grade

twin_rows.rule_middle_wall.reason: rule 7: a twin box's middle wall only where both carriageways and 0.6 m fit between the axes (spacing >= ca + cb + 0.6); else one wide cell; never a wall in a lane. Rows within 0.05 m of the threshold may go either way

checks_zero.reason: tunnelscan's fault rows within 40 m of the case's lines; a non-zero count is a known rest of the prototype (listed in check_rows), not a target

portal_end_profile.reason: the 20 m portal profile rule as a pure function (grading.portal_end_profile): exact
